parsed.restated: ∀ {s : ℝ}, 0 < s → s < 1 → (∀ {r : ℕ} {R : ℝ} (a : Fin (r + 1) → ℝ) (b : Fin r → ℝ), MetricCodes.Spherical.HigherHierarchy.Interlacing a b → s < 2 * MetricCodes.Spherical.HigherHierarchy.Gamma a b → MetricCodes.Spherical.HigherHierarchy.Phi a b < R → ∃ N : ℕ, ∀ n : ℕ, N ≤ n → ∀ C : SpherePacking.SphericalCode n s, (C.points.card : ℝ) < (2 : ℝ) ^ (R * (n : ℝ))) ∧ MetricCodes.Spherical.HigherHierarchy.sphericalCodeRate s ≤ MetricCodes.Spherical.HigherHierarchy.closedHierarchyVariationalRate s
parsed.english: For every spherical-code parameter s with 0 < s < 1, the following two statements hold. First, for any interlacing pair (a, b) with s < 2·Γ(a, b) and any R > Φ(a, b), there is an N such that every n ≥ N and every spherical code in dimension n with inner-product bound s has fewer than 2^(R·n) points. Second, the exponential rate of spherical codes is at most the closed hierarchy variational rate.
parsed.why_clearer: It replaces the eventual-in-atTop quantifier with an explicit threshold N and 'for all n ≥ N', and it keeps the hypotheses 0 < s < 1 explicit in the statement.
